sites.name: HMAS Brisbane (Wreck)

s1.quote: Brisbane was sunk approximately 2.8 nautical miles (5.2 km; 3.2 mi) off the coast of Mudjimba , Sunshine Coast, Queensland , on 31 July 2005 in 27 metres (89 ft) of water.

s2.quote: Wreck certification is not a requirement to dive this site Depth ranges from 6 – 28 metres

s3.quote: The wreck lies in about 28m of water, with upper sections around 15-16m deep. … Divers, snorkellers and vessels need a Queensland Parks permit or written authority

access.value: Queensland Parks permit or written authority required (booked through licensed operators)

penetration.value: Large openings cut in the hull; interior only for suitably trained divers

summary.text: A former navy destroyer deliberately sunk in 2005 off Mudjimba to serve as an artificial reef. The upper decks sit around 15 m with the seabed near 28 m, so exterior sections suit certified divers while the interior needs wreck training. A park permit is required.

sites.depthNote: Upper decks about 15-16 m; seabed about 28 m
